name: Xi’an-Style Chile Oil

ingredients.name: black vinegar, preferably Shanxi black vinegar

instructions.primary_message: Cut the yellow onion crosswise into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Cut the lightly packed cilantro stems into 2-inch pieces. Peel the garlic.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ medium yellow onion
¼ cup lightly packed cilantro stems
5 medium cloves garlic

instructions.primary_message: In a medium heatproof bowl, combine chile flakes with 2 tablespoons oil. Stir with a large spoon until all the chile flakes are evenly moistened; set aside.

In a medium saucepan, combine onion, cilantro stems, garlic, and the remaining 1 1/2 cups oil and cook over medium heat until oil registers 160°C and aromatics are golden and fragrant, about 10 minutes. Using a spider skimmer or slotted spoon, remove and discard aromatics or save for another use.

Reduce heat to low and maintain oil temperature at about 160°C. Add star anise, Sichuan peppercorns, cinnamon, fennel seeds, and coriander seeds. Cook, stirring occasionally, until spices are golden and oil is fragrant, 5 to 10 minutes. Using a skimmer or slotted spoon, remove and discard spices or reserve for another use.

For the First Pour: Increase heat and bring infused, strained oil to 195°C. Remove from heat. Using a dry 57 g ladle, carefully ladle 113 g of hot oil evenly over the reserved chile and oil mixture, stirring constantly with a large spoon to distribute the heat evenly.
For the Second Pour: Let the remaining oil cool to 160°C, about 1 minute. Using the same ladle, carefully ladle another 113 g of the now 160°C oil over the chile and oil mixture, stirring constantly.
For the Third Pour: Let the remaining oil cool to 140°C, 3 to 5 minutes longer. Using the ladle, carefully pour the remaining 140°C oil into the chile-and-oil mixture, stirring constantly.
Stir in black vinegar and let sizzle. Stir in kosher salt, sugar, and toasted sesame seeds until evenly incorporated.

Let chili oil cool to room temperature, about 45 minutes, then transfer to a clean glass jar or airtight container. Use immediately, or refrigerate for up to 1 month. Stir well before serving so each spoonful includes both oil and chile sediment.

description: Make Xi’an-style chile oil inspired by my grandmother’s recipe. The three-pour method creates a fragrant, flavorful condiment that’s delicious on noodles, dumplings, eggs, vegetables, and more.
notes:
Notes: At Chinese markets or online, look for chile flakes labeled 秦椒辣椒面 (ground Qin chiles) or 油泼辣子专用辣椒面 (ground chiles for oil-splashed chili). If you can’t find Qin chile, a blend of Sichuan er jing tiao (二荆条) and Xinjiang long chile (新疆辣椒) makes a very good substitute: er jing tiao brings fragrance and deep red color, while Xinjiang long chile adds gentle sweetness, body, and mild, fruity heat. For easier-to-find U.S. market alternatives, guajillo chiles and gochugaru can also work well.

This recipe makes enough to fill a pint-size jar. The method is best suited to a small batch: After the first pour, you can simply keep the remaining oil in the pot off the heat and let it cool between pours. For larger batches, divide the infused oil into three portions and heat them in separate pots to their target temperatures simultaneously to avoid what would otherwise be a much lengthier cool-down period.

Make-ahead and storage: Refrigerate chile oil in an airtight container for up to 1 month.
author: Qi Ai
